newsitem.title: EGYPT: Sudanese tribes make truce after 60 killed.
newsitem.headline: Sudanese tribes make truce after 60 killed.

text.p: Two tribes in western Sudan have signed a truce after fighting in which newspapers reported between 60 and 100 people killed last month.

Representatives of the Zaghawa and Reizegat tribes signed the agreement in the presence of an emissary from Khartoum and the governor of South Darfur state, Abdelhalim al-Mutaafi, the government newspaper al-Sudan al-Hadith said on Friday.
The tribes, which live in the far west of Sudan close to the border with Chad, have been fighting over water and grazing rights. They also accuse each other of armed robbery.
Three villages have been burnt down and 15,000 people displaced as a result of the clashes.
Under the agreement, the two sides will stop fighting as the prelude to a full reconciliation conference.
